title: VBCDX tool declaration (vbcdx.json)
description: Shipped at the root of an MCP tool package. Tells `vbcdx install tool` how to register the package's MCP server with a harness. It names things (the bin, its subcommands, the environment variables it reads) and is built so it cannot hold a host, a key or a token: arguments are lowercase words and --flags with no digits, and descriptions refuse URLs, host names, IP addresses and key-like runs. A description is free text, so a secret made only of ordinary words cannot be ruled out. Every per-field rule is in this schema. Six rules span fields and are checked only by the reference validator (src/install/tool-declaration.js, exported as validateToolDeclaration): http.port_env must be listed in env, and its modes (if given) include http; a variable whose modes list http needs an http mode; env names are unique, stdio.bin is a key of the package.json bin map, and in each args list no subcommand follows a --flag. Validate with validateToolDeclaration, not with this schema alone.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editors: a relative path ending in vbcdx-tool.schema.json. No URL, so it can never carry a host or credentials.

server_name.description: The MCP server name registered with the harness. Agents see its tools as mcp__<server_name>__<tool>, so it uses lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only.

contract.description: Optional interface contract the tool manifest declares, for example vbcdx.forgejo/1.

stdio.description: How the harness starts the server over stdio: the package bin and its arguments. The bin must be a key of the package's package.json bin map.

http.description: Optional network (Streamable HTTP) mode. The port is user config, named by port_env; no host or port value is declared.

path.description: URL path of the MCP endpoint, for example /mcp. No '.' or '..' segment.

port_env.description: Name of the environment variable that sets the listen port. It must also be listed in env.

env.description: Every environment variable the server reads, by name only, with a one-line description. Names are unique.

description.description: One line of printable text saying what the variable is for (no control characters, no line or paragraph separators, no invisible formatting characters such as bidi controls, zero-width characters or the soft hyphen). Never a value: no URL (://), no host name or IP address, no run of 20+ key characters (letters, digits, + / = -) and no run of 32+ including underscores. Plain words cannot be ruled out.

kind.description: credential: a secret the user supplies (written only as a ${VAR} reference); config: a non-secret setting.

required.description: True when the server cannot make a call without it.

modes.description: Optional. The run modes that read the variable: stdio (the server a harness starts) and http (the network server). Both when absent. A harness's stdio entry only carries the variables whose modes include stdio.

credential_file.description: Optional. Present when each tool call takes an absolute credential file path as an argument (the per-role identity); argument is that argument's name. vbcdx binds roles before the file exists, because some tools pass credentials through, so the tool itself must fail a call whose file is missing, unreadable or incomplete with an error that names the file and says what it must contain, never with a bare failure or by falling back to another identity. `vbcdx doctor` also reports a missing file.

manifest.description: Arguments that make the stdio bin print its JSON tool manifest and exit, for example ["manifest"].

args.description: Subcommands first, then bare --flags: lowercase letters joined by single hyphens, at most 31 characters, no digits, dots, '=' or '/'. No subcommand may follow a flag (validator rule), so a flag can never be given a value. These shapes leave no room for a host, key or token; a plain lowercase word is the only free text an argument can hold.
